cards.text: Last time, Saul blessed David and went home (1 Samuel 26:25). But I don't think David's unpacking his bags just yet, friend, because he says to himself, "One of these days now I will be swept away by the hand of Saul."

cards.question: David decides there's nothing better for him than to escape, so Saul will stop searching all over Israel. Where does he plan to go?

cards.text: So David and his six hundred men set out for Achish son of Maoch, the king of Gath, and settle there with their families. The LAST time David was in Gath, he pretended to be insane and let his spit run down his beard (1 Samuel 21:13), and now he's moving BACK?!

cards.question: David's two wives come with him to Gath. One is Ahinoam of Jezreel. Who's the other?
When Saul learns that David has fled to Gath, he keeps searching for him.

cards.text: Then David says to Achish, "If I have found favor in your eyes, let me be assigned a place in one of the outlying towns, so I can live there." Friend, that is the most polite way anybody has EVER asked to move out.

cards.question: David gives Achish a reason for wanting to live in one of the outlying towns. What is it?

answers.text: A servant shouldn't live in the royal city with the king
His men need open land for all their flocks
His family can't settle into a crowded city

cards.text: David asks for a spot in a town, and Achish hands him the WHOLE town: Ziklag. And the text says that to this day, it still belongs to the kings of Judah.

David lives in Philistine territory a year and four months, and in that time he and his men raid the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites. These people had lived since ancient times in the land stretching to Shur and Egypt.

cards.question: Whenever David attacks a territory, what does he take with him?

cards.text: This part's heavy, friend. He leaves no man or woman alive, and then he heads back to Achish.
Back in Gath, Achish asks him, "What have you raided today?" And David answers, "The Negev of Judah," or "The Negev of Jerahmeel," or "The Negev of the Kenites."

cards.question: David's raids hit the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites. When Achish asks what he raided, David tells him the truth.
David leaves no man or woman alive to be brought to Gath. He says that otherwise they would ___ him and his men.
After all of David's reports, Achish starts to suspect that David is lying to him.

cards.text: Achish trusts David, thinking, "Since he has made himself an utter stench to his people Israel, he will be my servant forever." Then the Philistines gather their forces for war against Israel. Uh-oh.

cards.question: With the Philistines gathering for war against Israel, what does Achish tell David?

answers.text: He and his men will go to battle with Achish
He and his men will stay behind and guard Gath
He and his men must leave Philistine land for now

cards.text: And David answers, "Then you will come to know what your servant can do." Friend, I've read that line TEN times, and I still can't tell you whose side it's promising to help.

cards.question: Achish already thinks David will be his servant forever. Now David says he'll show what he can do. So Achish makes David his ___ for life.

cards.text: The bodyguard of a Philistine king, with a war against Israel on the way. We'll stop right there, friend, but trust me, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the sentence about Achish trusting David, the sentence about the Philistines gathering for war, and the standalone "Uh-oh." Non-opening story cards are limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card tells both about the coming war against Israel (1 Samuel 28:1) and David's appointment as bodyguard (1 Samuel 28:2), but it cites only 1 Samuel 28:2. Its citation should cover 1 Samuel 28:1-2.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
